text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key rule is to follow clear naming conventions, so variables and functions describe exactly what they do. For example, a name like "calculateTotal" is much better than "x". You should also keep functions small and focused on one task, which makes them easier to test. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain, because future changes and bug fixes take less time when the structure is simple and organised. In short, writing clean code saves everyone effort in the long run.
